title: I Used the Ferry Bicycle-Lane Camera After They Blocked the Ramp

parts.text: I rolled to the 5:10 ferry and a pickup sat across the bike ramp with hazards on. The ramp sign the deckhand posted said: BIKES LOAD FIRST. NO HAZARDS ON THE RAMP. I was thirty-five, commuter, holding a clip card. Driver called it a two-minute grocery. I photographed the plate, the sign, and the blocked tires. Then I used the ferry camera QR the sign advertised and filed the still. At 5:12 the mate asked why that plate was on a ramp-block ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The mate can see a pickup on the bike ramp against the bikes-first sign.

social.video_title: A pickup sat hazards-on across the bike ramp — Part 1/2
social.description: 5:10 clip card, a grocery excuse, and a ramp camera QR. I filed the still. Would you have carried the bike up stairs?

parts.text: They called it a second until the mate waved them to car hold. I kept the ticket, the sign, and the photo. Bikes loaded. The pickup made the next boat. They told the lot the sign was always about optics. Optics is a word drivers use when a QR exists. Ramp policy now has a second line: GROCERIES ARE NOT A LANE. I roll on. They wait. The steel finally has two wheels first.

social.video_title: Groceries are not a bike lane — Part 2/2
social.description: Ramp-block ticket, the next boat for the pickup, and a second line on the sign. Was two minutes ever a ferry?
